cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Community Helper Discovery Basket
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Explore helper props and photos to build job vocabulary.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children examine hats, tools, and helper cards from a basket and talk about who uses them.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Basket
Assorted helper props
Helper picture cards (printable)
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Fill basket with safe props from many jobs
Include diverse helper images
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.setup: Circle or small-group basket at child height.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Pull one item and wonder aloud who might use it
2. Invite children to try hats/props
3. Match a prop to a helper card if they choose
4. Share which helper they want to play today
5. Return props to basket
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Who might use this tool? What job helps our community?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Names helpers; matches tool to role; handles props safely.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No sharp tools; supervise small props.
teacherTips: Include library, mail, sanitation, grocery — not only emergency jobs.
observationPrompts: Names helpers; matches tool to role; handles props safely.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Low basket with mixed helper hats/tools and picture cards.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Helper Hat Parade
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: March while choosing helper roles and singing a neighborhood helper song.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children pick a helper hat/prop and parade to Helpers in Our Neighborhood / Wheels on the Bus.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.setup: Hats in a line; path marked with tape/cones.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Choose a helper prop
2. March on the path
3. Freeze and name your helper job
4. Switch props if desired
5. Thank-you bow together
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Names role; follows path; joins song.
teacherTips: Celebrate every job equally.
observationPrompts: Names role; follows path; joins song.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Community Places Map Talk
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Connect helpers to community places using a simple map/signs.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children place helper cards on a map or near place signs (clinic, library, market, post office, build zone).
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Map poster or floor map
Place signs (printable)
Helper cards
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Post signs at child height
Prepare sticky dots/clips
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.setup: Map on floor/wall with signs nearby.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Name places on the map
2. Choose a helper card
3. Decide where that helper works
4. Place card/sign together
5. Tell one way the helper helps
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Where does this helper work? How do they help?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Links helper to place; uses place words.
teacherTips: Accept multiple right answers (nurses in clinics/hospitals/schools).
observationPrompts: Links helper to place; uses place words.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Classroom floor/wall map with helper place signs and cards.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Healthcare Helpers Clinic
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Role-play caring healthcare helpers with gentle routines.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children take turns as patients, nurses, doctors, or caregivers using a play clinic.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Play doctor kit
Bandages
Clipboards
Clinic sign
Stuffed animals optional
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Stage clinic with waiting chairs
Review gentle touch rules
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Choose a clinic role
2. Check in a patient/stuffed animal
3. Use tools gently
4. Explain how you are helping
5. Switch roles
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: How can you help your patient feel safe?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Uses care language; takes turns; gentle touch.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No real medicines; keep tools clean/play-only.
teacherTips: Include veterinarians as animal healthcare helpers.
observationPrompts: Uses care language; takes turns; gentle touch.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Preschool clinic dramatic-play center with kit and waiting chairs.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Rescue Colors Process Collage
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Create open-ended collage inspired by rescue/safety helpers using color choices children control.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children use red/yellow/black/blue papers, tape, and drawing tools to make their own rescue-inspired art. No model to copy.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Construction paper bits
Glue sticks/tape
Crayons/markers
Smocks
Optional helper photos for inspiration only
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Set invitation tray — no finished sample craft
Post prompt: ‘Helpers who keep us safe’
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.setup: Art table with collage tray and blank paper.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Look briefly at helper photos (inspiration only)
2. Choose papers/colors freely
3. Tear, stick, and draw your own ideas
4. Tell about your helper art if you want
5. Place on drying rack — every piece looks different
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: What colors help tell your helper story?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Makes choices; describes idea; process focus over product.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: Glue sticks preferred; supervise scissors if offered to older preschoolers only.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.cleanupTips: Sort leftover paper into scrap box.
teacherTips: Do not show a teacher-made firefighter to copy.
observationPrompts: Makes choices; describes idea; process focus over product.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Art table invitation with red/yellow/black collage materials — no perfect final craft shown.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Helper Tools Exploration Table
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Investigate safe play tools and discuss which helpers might use them.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children explore oversized play tools and helper cards at a table, sorting by interest and talking about jobs.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Safe play tools
Helper cards
Trays
Magnifiers optional
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Set 4–5 tool trays
Add diverse helper cards
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Choose a tool to investigate
2. Describe what it does
3. Guess which helpers might use it
4. Optional: place near a helper card
5. Try another tool
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: What job might need this tool?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Describes function; connects to helper; collaborates.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: Play tools only; no real hammers/sharp objects.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.cleanupTips: Return tools to silhouettes on shelf.
teacherTips: Accept creative answers (tape measure → builder or tailor).
observationPrompts: Describes function; connects to helper; collaborates.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Table with play tools on trays beside helper cards.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Mail Carrier Post Office
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Practice writing/drawing messages and delivering mail around the room.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children create simple notes/pictures and deliver them to mailbox spots as mail carriers.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Envelopes
Paper
Stickers
Mailbags
Mailbox signs
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Create 3–4 mailbox spots
Stock writing tray
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Draw or dictate a note
2. Stamp/sticker envelope
3. Load mailbag
4. Deliver to a mailbox
5. Switch roles (writer/carrier)
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Who will receive your mail today?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Marks on paper; follows delivery route; uses role language.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No real stamps with sharp edges; walking feet on route.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.cleanupTips: Collect undelivered mail into ‘to sort’ bin.
teacherTips: Dictation counts as writing.
observationPrompts: Marks on paper; follows delivery route; uses role language.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Post office dramatic play with mailbags and mailbox signs.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Grocery Helper Market
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Role-play grocery helpers who stock, shop, and help customers.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children run a market: stockers, cashiers, baggers, and shoppers using play food.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Play food
Baskets
Register/clipboard
Shelves
Market sign
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Stock shelves messily so children can restock
Price tags optional
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Choose a market job
2. Stock or shop with a list (picture list OK)
3. Practice kind customer talk
4. Bag groceries
5. Rotate jobs
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: How can a grocery helper make shopping easier?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Uses job talk; sorts food; cooperates.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No real glass containers; allergy-aware pretend foods.
teacherTips: Highlight that grocery helpers keep communities fed.
observationPrompts: Uses job talk; sorts food; cooperates.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Play market with shelves, baskets, and cashier spot.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Build a Community Block City
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Build community places with blocks and label helper locations.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children construct roads and buildings, then add place signs for helpers.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Blocks
Cars
Place signs
Paper labels
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Clear large block area
Offer signs
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Plan a place to build (library/clinic/road)
2. Build with a partner
3. Add a place sign
4. Drive/walk helpers through city
5. Tour the class city
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Which helpers work in your building?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Builds with purpose; collaborates; labels places.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: Height limits for block towers; walk around builds.
teacherTips: Invite construction helper language (hard hat, blueprint).
observationPrompts: Builds with purpose; collaborates; labels places.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Block city in progress with helper place signs.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Library Helper Story Center
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Practice library helper roles: choosing books, gentle handling, and story sharing.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children act as librarians and visitors — checking out books, stamping, and reading with friends.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Books
Checkout cards
Stamp/stickers
Library sign
Pillows
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Create simple checkout station
Display theme books
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Browse and choose a book
2. Check out with librarian helper
3. Read/look at pages with a friend
4. Return book to shelf marker
5. Recommend a book to someone
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: How do library helpers help us find stories?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Handles books gently; uses print concepts; recommends.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: Sitting feet in cozy area; no running with books.
teacherTips: Teachers are community helpers too — make that explicit.
observationPrompts: Handles books gently; uses print concepts; recommends.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Library corner with checkout desk and book display.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Sanitation Recycle Sort
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Sort clean recyclables/trash play items the way sanitation helpers keep communities clean.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children sort large clean items into recycle/trash/compost play bins and talk about helpers who collect them.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
3 bins with picture labels
Clean recyclable props
Gloves optional (play)
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Use only clean safe props
Label bins clearly
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Name each bin
2. Pick an item and decide
3. Sort into bin
4. Count how many in a bin
5. Thank sanitation helpers in chant
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Where should this go to help our community stay clean?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Sorts with reason; counts; uses helper language.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No glass/broken items; wash hands after.
teacherTips: Honor sanitation workers explicitly — often overlooked.
observationPrompts: Sorts with reason; counts; uses helper language.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Three labeled bins with large clean recyclable props.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Thank-You Helper Studio
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Create open-ended thank-you cards/pictures for community helpers.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children choose materials to make thank-you messages — dictated words OK. Products will all look different.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Cardstock
Crayons/markers
Stickers
Collage scraps
Dictation clipboard
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Set materials buffet
No sample card to copy
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Choose a helper to thank
2. Create with materials you pick
3. Dictate a message if you want
4. Sign with name/symbol
5. Place in ‘mail to helpers’ basket
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: What do you want your helper to know?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Chooses helper; marks with meaning; expresses thanks.
teacherTips: Process over pretty — display all.
observationPrompts: Chooses helper; marks with meaning; expresses thanks.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Card-making materials buffet without a model card.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Helper Interview Circle
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Ask and answer simple questions about helper jobs.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Children interview peers in helper roles using picture prompt cards.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Microphone prop
Prompt cards (printable)
Helper hats optional
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Model one interview
2. Child chooses a helper role
3. Peer asks a prompt question
4. Answer in a sentence/word
5. Clap thank-you
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: What tools do you use in your job?
teacherTips: Accept one-word answers.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Community Helper Obstacle Course
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Course stations: deliver mail, step through ‘build zone’, balance like a careful helper, recycle toss.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Cones
Tunnel/beans
Beanbags
Mailbox prop
Bins
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.preparation:
Set 4 stations outdoors/indoors
Demonstrate safe moves
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Preview stations
2. Deliver mail to mailbox
3. Move through build zone carefully
4. Recycle beanbag toss
5. High-five finish
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Helpers move carefully when they work!
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Navigates path; follows station ideas; safe body.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.safetyNotes: No racing requirement; spot climbing if used.
teacherTips: Emphasize careful helping over speed.
observationPrompts: Navigates path; follows station ideas; safe body.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.imageBriefSetup: Outdoor helper obstacle course with labeled stations.

cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.title: Community Helpers Celebration
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.objective: Review favorite helpers and celebrate with thank-you chant.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.description: Class reviews the week’s helpers, shares favorites, and sings Thank You Helpers Chant.
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.materials:
Helper cards
Thank-you basket of cards
Song chart
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.steps:
1. Recall helpers from the week
2. Share a favorite
3. Show thank-you art basket
4. Sing chant
5. Send family connection reminder
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.teacherLanguage: Which helper are you thankful for today?
cur-lp-preschool-community-helpers:item-.observationOpportunities: Recalls roles; participates in chant; gratitude talk.
teacherTips: Name overlooked helpers again (sanitation, grocery, library).
observationPrompts: Recalls roles; participates in chant; gratitude talk.

week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers explore many people who help a community — healthcare, fire/rescue, mail, grocery, construction, library, sanitation, and teachers — through dramatic play, process art, movement, and conversation. Anyone can do these jobs.
week.objectives:
Name a variety of community helpers and what they do
Use helper vocabulary in dramatic play
Practice cooperation and gratitude
Explore tools/places helpers use through play (not worksheets)
Create process-based art inspired by helpers (child-directed results)
week.weeklyMaterials:
Helper hats/vests (assorted roles)
Doctor kit (play)
Mailbags, envelopes, stickers
Play food / grocery props
Safe construction tools (plastic) + blocks
Library props (books, stamp, cards)
Recycle/sort bins
Collage materials (red/yellow/black/blue paper, tape, glue sticks)
Helper picture cards (printable draft)
Community map / place signs (printable draft)
week.familyConnection: Invite families to name one helper they noticed this week (no need to visit). Optional photo of a helper place from the neighborhood.
week.adaptations: Offer picture cards for vocabulary. Dictate thank-you messages. Provide quieter helper stations. Present diverse photos of helpers of many genders/backgrounds.
week.vocabularyWords:
helper
community
job
tool
safe
thank you
deliver
care
build
serve
recycle
library
mail
grocery
week.teacherPreparation:
Stage dramatic-play areas for 2–3 helper roles (rotate midweek)
Print helper cards and place signs (draft)
Set process-art collage tray (no sample final craft to copy)

monday.objectives:
Explore helper props
March as helpers
Talk about helper places on a map
monday.materials:
Helper hats/vests (assorted roles)
Doctor kit (play)
Mailbags, envelopes, stickers
Play food / grocery props
Safe construction tools (plastic) + blocks
Library props (books, stamp, cards)
Recycle/sort bins
Collage materials (red/yellow/black/blue paper, tape, glue sticks)
Helper picture cards (printable draft)
Community map / place signs (printable draft)
monday.vocabulary:
helper
community
job
tool
safe
thank you
deliver
care
build
serve
recycle
library
mail
grocery
circleTime: Read Whose Hands Are These? excerpt
monday.outdoorPlay: Outdoor helper march and ‘delivery’ pathways with cones.
monday.adaptations: Offer picture cards for vocabulary. Dictate thank-you messages. Provide quieter helper stations. Present diverse photos of helpers of many genders/backgrounds.
monday.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and active games; allergy-aware art materials; keep pathways clear.

items.cleanupTips: Return tools to silhouettes on shelf.
teacherTips: Accept creative answers (tape measure → builder or tailor).
items.imageBriefSetup: Table with play tools on trays beside helper cards.

items.title: Mail Carrier Post Office
items.objective: Practice writing/drawing messages and delivering mail around the room.
items.description: Children create simple notes/pictures and deliver them to mailbox spots as mail carriers.
items.materials:
Envelopes
Paper
Stickers
Mailbags
Mailbox signs
items.preparation:
Create 3–4 mailbox spots
Stock writing tray
items.steps:
1. Draw or dictate a note
2. Stamp/sticker envelope
3. Load mailbag
4. Deliver to a mailbox
5. Switch roles (writer/carrier)
items.teacherLanguage: Who will receive your mail today?
items.observationOpportunities: Marks on paper; follows delivery route; uses role language.
items.safetyNotes: No real stamps with sharp edges; walking feet on route.
items.cleanupTips: Collect undelivered mail into ‘to sort’ bin.
teacherTips: Dictation counts as writing.
items.imageBriefSetup: Post office dramatic play with mailbags and mailbox signs.

items.title: Grocery Helper Market
items.objective: Role-play grocery helpers who stock, shop, and help customers.
items.description: Children run a market: stockers, cashiers, baggers, and shoppers using play food.
items.materials:
Play food
Baskets
Register/clipboard
Shelves
Market sign
items.preparation:
Stock shelves messily so children can restock
Price tags optional
items.steps:
1. Choose a market job
2. Stock or shop with a list (picture list OK)
3. Practice kind customer talk
4. Bag groceries
5. Rotate jobs
items.teacherLanguage: How can a grocery helper make shopping easier?
items.observationOpportunities: Uses job talk; sorts food; cooperates.
items.safetyNotes: No real glass containers; allergy-aware pretend foods.
teacherTips: Highlight that grocery helpers keep communities fed.
items.imageBriefSetup: Play market with shelves, baskets, and cashier spot.

items.title: Build a Community Block City
items.objective: Build community places with blocks and label helper locations.
items.description: Children construct roads and buildings, then add place signs for helpers.
items.materials:
Blocks
Cars
Place signs
Paper labels
items.preparation:
Clear large block area
Offer signs
items.steps:
1. Plan a place to build (library/clinic/road)
2. Build with a partner
3. Add a place sign
4. Drive/walk helpers through city
5. Tour the class city
items.teacherLanguage: Which helpers work in your building?
items.observationOpportunities: Builds with purpose; collaborates; labels places.
items.safetyNotes: Height limits for block towers; walk around builds.
teacherTips: Invite construction helper language (hard hat, blueprint).
items.imageBriefSetup: Block city in progress with helper place signs.

items.title: Library Helper Story Center
items.objective: Practice library helper roles: choosing books, gentle handling, and story sharing.
items.description: Children act as librarians and visitors — checking out books, stamping, and reading with friends.
items.materials:
Books
Checkout cards
Stamp/stickers
Library sign
Pillows
items.preparation:
Create simple checkout station
Display theme books
items.steps:
1. Browse and choose a book
2. Check out with librarian helper
3. Read/look at pages with a friend
4. Return book to shelf marker
5. Recommend a book to someone
items.teacherLanguage: How do library helpers help us find stories?
items.observationOpportunities: Handles books gently; uses print concepts; recommends.
items.safetyNotes: Sitting feet in cozy area; no running with books.
teacherTips: Teachers are community helpers too — make that explicit.
items.imageBriefSetup: Library corner with checkout desk and book display.

items.title: Sanitation Recycle Sort
items.objective: Sort clean recyclables/trash play items the way sanitation helpers keep communities clean.
items.description: Children sort large clean items into recycle/trash/compost play bins and talk about helpers who collect them.
items.materials:
3 bins with picture labels
Clean recyclable props
Gloves optional (play)
items.preparation:
Use only clean safe props
Label bins clearly
items.steps:
1. Name each bin
2. Pick an item and decide
3. Sort into bin
4. Count how many in a bin
5. Thank sanitation helpers in chant
items.teacherLanguage: Where should this go to help our community stay clean?
items.observationOpportunities: Sorts with reason; counts; uses helper language.
items.safetyNotes: No glass/broken items; wash hands after.
teacherTips: Honor sanitation workers explicitly — often overlooked.
items.imageBriefSetup: Three labeled bins with large clean recyclable props.

items.title: Thank-You Helper Studio
items.objective: Create open-ended thank-you cards/pictures for community helpers.
items.description: Children choose materials to make thank-you messages — dictated words OK. Products will all look different.
items.materials:
Cardstock
Crayons/markers
Stickers
Collage scraps
Dictation clipboard
items.preparation:
Set materials buffet
No sample card to copy
items.steps:
1. Choose a helper to thank
2. Create with materials you pick
3. Dictate a message if you want
4. Sign with name/symbol
5. Place in ‘mail to helpers’ basket
items.teacherLanguage: What do you want your helper to know?
items.observationOpportunities: Chooses helper; marks with meaning; expresses thanks.
teacherTips: Process over pretty — display all.
items.imageBriefSetup: Card-making materials buffet without a model card.

items.title: Helper Interview Circle
items.objective: Ask and answer simple questions about helper jobs.
items.description: Children interview peers in helper roles using picture prompt cards.
items.materials:
Microphone prop
Prompt cards (printable)
Helper hats optional
items.steps:
1. Model one interview
2. Child chooses a helper role
3. Peer asks a prompt question
4. Answer in a sentence/word
5. Clap thank-you
items.teacherLanguage: What tools do you use in your job?
teacherTips: Accept one-word answers.

items.title: Community Helper Obstacle Course
items.description: Course stations: deliver mail, step through ‘build zone’, balance like a careful helper, recycle toss.
items.materials:
Cones
Tunnel/beans
Beanbags
Mailbox prop
Bins
items.preparation:
Set 4 stations outdoors/indoors
Demonstrate safe moves
items.steps:
1. Preview stations
2. Deliver mail to mailbox
3. Move through build zone carefully
4. Recycle beanbag toss
5. High-five finish
items.teacherLanguage: Helpers move carefully when they work!
items.observationOpportunities: Navigates path; follows station ideas; safe body.
items.safetyNotes: No racing requirement; spot climbing if used.
teacherTips: Emphasize careful helping over speed.
items.imageBriefSetup: Outdoor helper obstacle course with labeled stations.

items.title: Community Helpers Celebration
items.objective: Review favorite helpers and celebrate with thank-you chant.
items.description: Class reviews the week’s helpers, shares favorites, and sings Thank You Helpers Chant.
items.materials:
Helper cards
Thank-you basket of cards
Song chart
items.steps:
1. Recall helpers from the week
2. Share a favorite
3. Show thank-you art basket
4. Sing chant
5. Send family connection reminder
items.teacherLanguage: Which helper are you thankful for today?
items.observationOpportunities: Recalls roles; participates in chant; gratitude talk.
teacherTips: Name overlooked helpers again (sanitation, grocery, library).
